overview: This bill requires the Small Business Administration (SBA), the federal agency that supports small companies, to share information about individual coverage health reimbursement arrangements, known as ICHRAs. An ICHRA lets an employer give workers tax-free money to buy their own individual health insurance instead of offering a traditional group plan. The SBA would pass along information prepared by agencies such as the Treasury, Health and Human Services, and Labor departments through its local district offices and small business development centers. It would also include the information in its social media, press releases and website. As of July 2, 2026, a House committee had approved it, and a supplemental committee report had been filed.
for: Supporters say many small business owners don't know ICHRAs exist, and spreading the word could help more of them offer health benefits to their workers.
against: Critics say the bill only promotes one type of health benefit rather than explaining all options, and ICHRAs can shift workers onto individual insurance markets where costs and coverage vary.
